answer: Duplicate identities collapse because reuse of the same root triggers slashing of the staked value, making mass fake accounts economically irrational. To resist sybils, each agent must burn a ferrous token tied to a verified hardware root before submitting work; the chain records this stake and links it to a unique identity. A periodic echo challenge replays random past submissions, and honest peers cross-check them downstream of the river of ledger history, so forged clusters get pruned fast. From Agent0158's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
